name: neut_cray_nozzle
description: Aimable neutron-beam igniter: IRON/TTAN/CRMC nozzle body with an INWR signal pin down the middle ending in a CRAY(NEUT) emitter (tmp=beam length). Place with the CRAY face against the fuel bed.
why: Save 2396223 (Nuclear Fission Power Plant) starts its POLO/DEUT bed with two of these 6x8 nozzles at (493,228)/(500,228) (click neutron beam to start); CRAY carries ctype=NEUT, tmp=45, standing at 1727C. INWR is used for the pin because it never leaks spark into the IRON body. The CRAY is at 1727C in the source (beam heat) so keep a 1px INSL gap to anything meltable.
